title: Enabling Real-Time AI for Scientific Instruments with GPU-Native Data Acquisition | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA and Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory's Molecular Foundry use DAQIRI, a Holoscan data-acquisition library, to stream a new high-dynamic-range EELS electron-microscopy camera's 500+ Gbps output directly into GPU memory for real-time processing. The new DAQIRI release adds NIC hardware packet reordering on ConnectX-7+, an ibverbs engine with ~2x per-core throughput vs DPDK at small packets, and a direct polling mode with 2-4 µs loopback latency.

insights.claim: A high-dynamic-range electron microscopy camera developed at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory's Molecular Foundry captures strong and faint EELS signals simultaneously, replacing the conventional two-pass acquisition but generating more than 500 Gbps of data, over 500x faster than conventional EELS data streams.
insights.speaker: Cara Laasch
insights.so_what: Next-gen scientific detectors are producing data rates that require GPU-attached acquisition, expanding NVIDIA's addressable market into instrumentation.
insights.quote: This is over 500x faster than conventional EELS data streams
insights.locator: This advancement simplifies the experimental setup

insights.claim: In the Berkeley Lab EELS pipeline, FPGA readout electronics send detector data over Ethernet, NVIDIA DAQIRI receives packets directly into GPU memory, and GPU processing assembles and corrects frames and reduces them to energy-loss spectra while the experiment runs, letting researchers adjust acquisition parameters in real time.
insights.speaker: Cara Laasch
insights.so_what: Template for GPU displacing custom FPGA/CPU processing in instrument data paths; watch for adoption by microscopy and detector vendors.
insights.locator: Handling that stream requires an acquisition

insights.claim: GPU computation in the Berkeley Lab pipeline enables submicron spatial resolution from sensor pixels measuring 5 micrometers across.
insights.speaker: Cara Laasch
insights.so_what: Compute is substituting for sensor hardware improvements, shifting instrument value toward software and GPUs.
insights.locator: Computation also improves the spatial information

insights.claim: NVIDIA argues that data-movement and processing limits currently shape how scientific instruments are designed, and that GPU-native acquisition lets instrument makers design around what will be measured rather than around those constraints.
insights.speaker: Cara Laasch
insights.so_what: If adopted, instrument makers become GPU platform customers at design time, a sticky edge-compute channel for NVIDIA.
insights.quote: Yet limits on how quickly the measured data can be moved and processed often shape how an instrument is designed
insights.locator: In science and industry, analyzing sensor measurements

insights.claim: DAQIRI can now offload packet reordering to NVIDIA ConnectX-7 or newer NICs, which parse sequence fields and place each payload directly in its ordered position in memory, removing a software reorder copy step and preserving CPU and GPU resources.
insights.speaker: Cara Laasch
insights.so_what: Ties DAQIRI's best features to ConnectX-7+ hardware, reinforcing NVIDIA's NIC attach in edge/science deployments.
insights.locator: Reorder data as it arrives with NIC hardware

insights.claim: DAQIRI's new ibverbs engine, built on libibverbs and NVIDIA DevX and now the default for raw Ethernet streams, delivers roughly twice the per-core throughput of the previous default DPDK backend at small packet sizes (up to 1024 bytes) and data rates above 200 Gbps, while 8 KB packet throughput is similar.
insights.speaker: Cara Laasch
insights.so_what: NVIDIA is moving away from DPDK toward its own verbs/DevX stack for high-rate ingest, deepening software lock-in to its NICs.
insights.locator: Use the ibverbs engine for efficient acquisition

insights.claim: The ibverbs engine benchmarks were run on NVIDIA DGX Spark, NVIDIA IGX Thor, and NVIDIA RTX PRO server platforms, indicating DAQIRI targets NVIDIA's edge and workstation-class systems.
insights.speaker: Cara Laasch
insights.so_what: Edge platforms like IGX Thor and DGX Spark are being positioned as instrument-side compute.
insights.locator: Use the ibverbs engine for efficient acquisition

insights.claim: DAQIRI's direct polling mode lets the application thread send and receive packets directly without handing off to a separate I/O worker, demonstrating application send-to-receive latency of about 2-4 µs in cabled loopback tests, and can be used for control queues while bulk data streams keep batched processing.
insights.speaker: Cara Laasch
insights.so_what: Microsecond-scale feedback loops enable closed-loop, AI-steered experiments and industrial control on GPU platforms.
insights.locator: Reduce feedback latency with direct polling
